business_summary: Visa runs the world's largest electronic payments network (VisaNet). It does NOT lend money or issue cards itself; banks issue Visa-branded cards and Visa simply moves the authorization and settlement messages between the shopper's bank and the merchant's bank. It earns a tiny fee on each transaction (data processing revenue), a fee on the dollar volume that flows across the network (service revenue), a higher-margin fee on cross-border/international payments, plus a fast-growing 'other revenue' line of value-added services (fraud tools, consulting, tokenization) - all partly offset by incentives paid to banks. In the quarter ended June 30, 2026 it processed 71.7 billion transactions. Volume rises with global consumer spending and the long migration from cash/checks to cards and digital payments, so revenue compounds with the economy plus the cash-to-card shift, at very high margins and almost no incremental cost per transaction.

moat.type: Network effect + global scale + brand + high switching costs; near-duopoly with Mastercard

valuation.method: Blend of two methods via code/valuation.py. (1) P/E: TTM GAAP diluted EPS $11.75 (FY2025 $10.20 - 9M FY2025 $7.59 + 9M FY2026 $9.14) x 25/29/33 = $293.75/$340.75/$387.75. A wide-moat near-duopoly compounder like Visa has historically earned a high-20s multiple, so 29x is the base. (2) FCF yield: TTM FCF/share $10.93 ($21.013B FCF / 1,923M TTM diluted shares) at 5.0%/4.2%/3.5% = $218.60/$260.24/$312.29. Average of the two = low $256.18 / base $300.49 / high $350.02. GAAP (not non-GAAP) EPS is used deliberately: Visa books a litigation provision in essentially every quarter ($1.290B in 9M FY2026), so we treat it as a real recurring cost. On TTM non-GAAP EPS of $12.77 the same 29x would imply ~$370, i.e. roughly today's price.

bull_case: Wide-moat near-duopoly: VisaNet's global network of issuers, merchants and acquirers across more than 200 countries is almost impossible to replicate; new entrants cannot match its acceptance footprint or trust.

Long secular tailwind: cash and checks are still a large share of global payments, giving Visa years of volume growth on top of GDP-linked consumer spending. Q3 FY2026 payments volume +10%, total cross-border volume +13%, processed transactions +10% (all constant-dollar).
Exceptional and still-improving economics: 60.7% TTM GAAP operating margin, ~38% ROIC, capex of only $1.567B on $44.5B of TTM revenue, and ~$21.0B of TTM free cash flow.
Growth is holding up better than expected: nine-month FY2026 net revenue +15.3% YoY, faster than the 10.9% three-year CAGR; Q3 FY2026 net revenue +14%.
Value-added services are scaling fast: Q3 FY2026 'other revenue' $1.496B, +45% YoY - the fastest-growing line and a genuine diversification away from pure swipe fees.

Fortress balance sheet (0.35x net debt/EBITDA) funding heavy shareholder returns: $16.430B of class A buybacks plus $3.852B of dividends in nine months, with $28.4B of buyback authorization still remaining at 2026-06-30, shrinking the share count (diluted class A 1,898M in Q3 FY2026 vs 1,959M a year earlier).

The long-running US merchant interchange overhang moved toward resolution: the court granted preliminary approval to the Visa/Mastercard settlement on 2026-06-09, and Visa's accrued litigation balance fell from $3.033B to $1.274B over the nine months.
Buying capability rather than renting it: the $2.4B all-cash BioCatch acquisition (announced 2026-08-03) deepens the AI fraud-detection moat that keeps Visa's network the trusted default.
risks: VALUATION IS THE MAIN RISK TODAY: at $370.47 the stock trades ~23% above our base fair value of $300.49 and above the high end of our band ($350.02). There is no margin of safety; on TTM GAAP EPS of $11.75 the stock is at ~31.5x trailing earnings.

Earnings growth decelerated sharply versus last quarter: Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS grew only 10% (and net income only 7%) versus +36% GAAP EPS in Q2 FY2026. The Q2 figure flattered a weak prior-year comparison; +10% is the more honest run-rate.

Cost growth is outrunning revenue: Q3 FY2026 GAAP operating expenses rose 19% (non-GAAP +17%) against 14% revenue growth, with personnel expense up from $1.749B to $2.458B. Operating margin fell from 60.7% to 59.1% year over year. Client incentives grew 18%, faster than revenue.

The highest-margin line is lagging its volume: Q3 FY2026 international transaction revenue grew only 6% to $3.853B even though cross-border volume ex-intra-Europe grew 12% constant-dollar - a sign that currency-volatility tailwinds are fading and/or pricing is being competed away.

The interchange settlement is not free: it trims credit interchange by 10 basis points for five years, caps standard consumer card rates at 1.25% for eight years, and gives merchants new rights to surcharge, steer and decline premium/commercial cards. Those steering rights could slow the growth of Visa's richest volume mix. Final approval and a threatened appeal to the 2nd Circuit are still ahead.

Balance sheet is less pristine than a year ago: net debt rose from ~$2.4B to ~$9.916B as Visa levered up modestly to fund buybacks; interest expense jumped to $194M in Q3 FY2026 from $39M a year earlier.
Disruption: account-to-account / real-time payment rails (FedNow, UPI, Pix), stablecoins, and Big Tech wallets could route volume around the card networks over time.
Cyclicality: consumer spending and especially high-margin cross-border travel volume fall in recessions.
Regulatory/antitrust remains perennial: interchange-fee caps and routing rules in the US and EU could compress network economics beyond the current settlement.
M&A execution: the $2.4B BioCatch deal is not expected to close until fiscal Q2 2027 and adds integration risk; goodwill and intangibles already total $48.4B of the $94.6B balance sheet.
what_would_break_thesis: GAAP operating margin falls below 50% for two consecutive fiscal quarters (erosion of the network's pricing power). Currently 59.1% in Q3 FY2026.
Net revenue shrinks year-over-year for two consecutive quarters outside a clearly identified macro recession (signals structural volume loss / disruption).
Net-debt-to-EBITDA rises above 2.0x (a sign of balance-sheet deterioration or value-destroying M&A). Currently ~0.35x - watch this, it has risen from ~0.1x in one year.
Free cash flow turns negative for a full fiscal year.
GAAP operating expenses grow faster than net revenue for four consecutive quarters (the cost discipline that produces the 60% margin has broken).
A regulatory ruling or settlement beyond the current MDL deal that structurally caps interchange/network fees in a major market (US or EU) and is expected to cut net revenue by more than ~15%.

Cross-border volume growth stalls structurally (not just one recession), or international transaction revenue declines year-over-year for two consecutive quarters, indicating a permanent loss of the highest-margin business.
Processed transaction growth falls below ~3% year-over-year for two consecutive quarters outside a recession (evidence that A2A rails or stablecoins are taking share).
A serious accounting red flag or restatement.
catalysts: Q4 and full-year FY2026 earnings, expected late October 2026 (FY ends 2026-09-30) - watch the cross-border/international transaction revenue gap and whether operating expense growth normalises after the $563M severance charge.
Final approval hearing in the US merchant interchange settlement, and the threatened appeal to the 2nd Circuit - a clean final approval would remove a two-decade overhang.
Closing of the $2.4B BioCatch acquisition, expected in fiscal Q2 2027.
Continued execution of the $28.4B remaining buyback authorization shrinking the share count.
Continued scaling of value-added services / 'other revenue' (+45% YoY in Q3 FY2026) as a larger share of the mix.
